input.summary:
P1 dining room (parts/room-11.mjs) is designed and checks OK in a scratch copy: a centre table (oak fence and top slab) with one north stair chair, a barrel sideboard with a potted poppy in the NE corner, and one hanging lantern over the table. Walk is 8/8 reachable, light min 11, FIT OK.
In the real make.sh the part lands 0 cells: shell-west fills the whole interior with air, runParts counts that as earlier-part ownership, and all 6 of my writes were REFUSED. The build still saves a whole build.nbt.
Not fixed: the lock conflicts with the spec's "build only into air", so every room part will hit it. Fix belongs in parts/shell-west.mjs (stop writing interior air) or in runParts (lock only non-air cells); both are outside my module.
left: make.sh refuses all 6 writes of room-11 (27,2,15 / 27,3,15 / 27,2,14 / 28,2,14 / 28,3,14 / 27,4,15) because shell-west.mjs lines 16, 20 and 23 fill the room interior with air and runParts treats that air as owned. Needs the shell owner to stop writing interior air, or runParts to lock only non-air cells. Once that is fixed, re-run ./make.sh: the part should then land as written.

Verified only in a scratch copy (/tmp/part18-test/try.nbt, built by applying build() directly to build.nbt without runParts): room check OK, render reads as a table with chair and sideboard. Not verified in the official build.

Single chair (north side) instead of the full set: the south chair cell is the lane that connects the west doorways to the east doorways, so only one chair fits the walk rule in a 3 x 3 room. Owner may want a second chair if the room grows.
plan.md checklist and elements.md not ticked: the part did not land in the real build.

waste.what: Worked out by hand which interior cells are doorway first-cells (the lane rule) on a 3 x 3 room, one cell at a time, to find where a table and chair fit without splitting the room.
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of reasoning and 2 scratch-test runs
waste.tool: mcd plan could mark which free cells are doorway first-cells and which keep a lane open between doorways, so the chair and table slots are visible at once.
